digest_algorithm: sha256 over the file's bytes with CRLF normalised to LF
what_this_records: The successor pin for scripts/match_signatures.py, recorded by the dated amendment `transliteration.prereg.v1.amendment.exact-literals-2026-08-24` in the SAME commit that changes the parser.

It exists because a pin cannot be edited underneath the artifacts that quoted it. experiments/transliteration_prereg.json keeps the digest the v0.19 transliteration run was measured under; this file carries the digest every FUTURE comparison is read against.
A revalidator resolves a retired row by following its amendment to this file. The chain is followed, never skipped: a marker naming an amendment its own prereg does not record fails loudly.

the_change.what: match_signatures.Parser built numeric literals as ('num', float(tok)); an INTEGER surface is now ('num', int(tok)) through match_signatures.exact_literal. A decimal surface stays float.
the_change.why: Every literal wider than a double's 53-bit significand was destroyed at parse time. Two ground statements were served the right verdict with printed values wrong by 4.4e59, returned as an exact Fraction so nothing downstream could tell — while v0.18's numeral pair refused those same two statements by name. One subsystem refused honestly; the other silently corrupted.
the_change.scope_verified_not_assumed: Skeletons and shape keys are byte-identical across the change for all 25,554 committed terms (both canonical_ascii and anonymized_template, every corpus). int and Fraction format under ':g' exactly as float did, which is why no twin group, decomposition or specialization moves. The evidence is experiments/exact_literals_served_diff.json.
why_decimals_stay_float: Every destroyed literal measured is an integer; a decimal under this tokenizer is short enough for a double.

Making decimals Fraction was tried first and the served-line diff REFUSED it: 199 statements lost their `in words` line, because numeral_words.number_to_words accepts int and float and rejects a Fraction as 'not a number'.
Widening that would retire the pinned numeral pair as well and move R2's registered numeral domain — a separate decision needing its own registration, not something to smuggle into this one.

amendments_within_this_prereg.reason: H1 (adversarial review): §4b's exact integer literals put an uncaught OverflowError on a served route. `f"{value:g}"` never raises on a float but must convert an int to float first, so a literal past a double's range traced out of route_line instead of returning a verdict, and the HTTP skin dropped the connection. `match_signatures.format_num` guards the three key builders and emits exactly what the float path emitted.
amendments_within_this_prereg.why_the_pin_moves_rather_than_a_new_prer: The retirement this file records is unchanged — the parser is still the successor pin for the row transliteration_prereg retired. This is a correction to the successor's own bytes, dated inside the successor rather than pretending the original pin was always this value.

experiments/exact_literals_served_diff.json findings byte-identical: answer lines moved 0 of 14,830, evaluate route moved 3, same three statement ids. Only the recorded parser digest and the before-blob provenance string differ.

read_this_row_as: The digest this row records is the parser AS THE v0.20 EXACT-LITERAL LANE MEASURED IT, and it is left byte-unchanged for exactly that reason: experiments/exact_literals_served_diff.json quotes a before/after served-line diff taken through it, and a pin edited underneath an artifact cannot be checked at all.

It is no longer the pin a FUTURE comparison is read against. The successor pin is the `parser` row of experiments/big_op_disclosure_prereg.json, recorded by the amendment named above in the SAME commit that changes the parser and BEFORE any artifact quotes a number measured through it.
So this row is history, not a live gate: a revalidator checks the successor pin against the tree and this one against the artifacts that quoted it.

why: ROADMAP-v0.20 4c moved this file's subprocess timeouts, which drifted the pin foreign_voice.prereg.v1 froze at 0db59b36. The batch review's M6 ordered the drift declared rather than inherited, so this registry -- already the terminal book for the parser the same batch moved -- carries the successor pin for the second moved file too. One retirement batch, one terminal registry.

Third moved pin to land here (parser 4b, hermetic_rule 4c review M6, evaluator v0.21): this registry's original one-batch scope is WIDENED by this dated note to serve as the terminal pin book for moved conformance-frozen modules generally, because one registry with a walkable chain beats one registry per move.

non_claims: Not a claim that every literal is exact END TO END. It fixes destruction AT PARSE TIME for integers. float('0.1') is still not exactly one tenth, so an evaluator that must decide 0.1 + 0.2 = 0.3 needs the numeral domain widened first. Filed, not fixed here.

Not a claim that BACKLOG's node list was right. Its 3 nodes included leanworkbook.skel.lean_workbook_50397, whose `inf` is frozen into the committed anonymized_template by scripts/seed_lean_workbook.py and whose canonical_ascii does not tokenize — the parser never sees it, so this change cannot repair it. That node needs a seed regeneration under AGENTS.md's seeds-are-the-source-of-truth rule and is filed rather than smuggled into a parser commit. In its place the served diff surfaced goedelpset.skel.goedel_pset_789185. Three served nodes are repaired, but not the same three.
Not a security fix. Loopback-only, single user, nothing untrusted reaches the path (ROADMAP-v0.20 §4's own note).
Not a performance claim of any kind.

Not a claim that a skeleton KEY can represent a literal past a double's range. A node keyed `inf` is a node whose literal is unrecoverable IN THE KEY, even though §4b made the parsed value exact. Skeletons are a structural index, not a value channel; widening them is a corpus-wide change with its own seal, and format_num deliberately reproduces the prior key rather than improving it.

why: The v0.25 adversarial design review (docs/DESIGN-house-rules.md §4, docs/ROADMAP-v0.25.md §2) found a silent-capture hazard in this parser. `parse_atom`'s big-operator branch rewrites any identifier whose lowercase begins `sum_ / prod_ / lim_ / max_ / min_` into a bare operator call, keeping only the part before the first underscore. `sum_total(x)` and `sum_anything(x)` therefore produced one identical tree, the authored suffix was discarded, and no refusal or record existed anywhere.

The acceptance frozen in ROADMAP-v0.25 §2 is `a refusal or a disclosure, never a silent rewrite`. The corpus census decided the arm rather than a preference: 17 of the 14,830 committed anonymized_template strings carry a big-op identifier (16 `sum_i`, 1 `lim_h`, no `prod_`/`max_`/`min_`), so a refusal would break sealed committed parses that are not defective. The lane ships DISCLOSURE.

The disclosure is total and judgement-free: every capture is recorded, `sum_i` as loudly as `sum_total`. Disclosing only the captures that look wrong would need an authored rule for what looks wrong, which this lane did not price and which DESIGN-house-rules §4 explicitly leaves to H-P0's declaration-boundary prefix guard.

Not one parse tree moved. Skeletons, shape keys, twin groups, decompositions and specializations are byte-identical across the change; the only ledger bytes that move are the new `parse_rewrites` disclosure and the provenance digest that tracks the writer. That is what makes this a pin movement and not a measurement movement.

THREE assertions are re-aimed by hand, each citing this amendment at the assertion — the discipline the 2026-08-24 transliteration amendment recorded, and the reason it recorded it: a test re-aimed without an amendment to cite is a test edited to make a change pass. (1) tests/test_transliteration.py's expected chain END moves from exact_literals to this successor; the assertion beside it, that the terminal pin equals the tree, is untouched and is what actually checks. (2) The same file's corrupt-successor fixture is rebuilt to corrupt the chain's NEW terminal pin and to walk both hops inside its temp root, because corrupting the middle of a three-hop chain proves nothing. The retirement is followed, never skipped: a marker naming an amendment its own prereg does not record fails loudly rather than dropping the check. Both re-aimed suites carry a test asserting exactly that, so the weakening cannot be widened silently.
